display_title: 20-3-2 地球上的珊瑚礁还有救吗？

sentences.en: Conservationists have put the final touches to a giant artificial reef they have been assembling at the world-renowned Zoological Society of London (London Zoo).
sentences.zh: 在世界闻名的伦敦动物学会（伦敦动物园），自然保护工作者已经为他们一直在搭建的一座巨型人工珊瑚礁完成了收尾工作。

sentences.en: Samples of the planet’s most spectacular corals – vivid green branching coral, yellow scroll, blue ridge and many more species – have been added to the giant tank along with fish that thrive in their presence: blue tang, clownfish and many others.
sentences.zh: 地球上一些最壮观的珊瑚品种的样本，包括鲜绿色的枝状珊瑚、黄色卷叶珊瑚、蓝脊珊瑚等，已经被放入这个巨大的水族缸。一同入缸的还有蓝刺尾鱼、小丑鱼等许多在珊瑚间生长良好的鱼。

sentences.en: The reef is in the zoo’s new gallery, Tiny Giants, which is dedicated to the minuscule invertebrate creatures that sustain life across the planet.
sentences.zh: 这座珊瑚礁位于动物园新建的“微小的巨人”展馆，展馆专门介绍那些维系着全球生命的微小无脊椎动物。

sentences.en: The coral reef tank and its seven-metre-wide window form the core of the exhibition.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚礁水族缸和它七米宽的观景窗构成了展览的核心。

sentences.en: ‘Coral reefs are the most diverse ecosystems on Earth and we want to show people how wonderful they are,’ said Paul Pearce-Kelly, senior curator of invertebrates and fish at the Zoological Society of London.
sentences.zh: “珊瑚礁是地球上生物多样性最高的生态系统，我们想让人们看到它们有多么奇妙，”伦敦动物学会无脊椎动物和鱼类高级馆员保罗·皮尔斯-凯利说。

sentences.en: ‘However, we also want to highlight the research and conservation efforts that are now being carried out to try to save them from the threat of global warming.’
sentences.zh: “不过，我们也想突出展示目前开展的研究与保护工作，人们正努力使珊瑚礁免受全球变暖的威胁。”

sentences.en: They want people to see what is being done to try to save these wonders.
sentences.zh: 他们想让人们看到，为了挽救这些自然奇观，人们正在做些什么。

sentences.en: Corals are composed of tiny animals, known as polyps, with tentacles for capturing small marine creatures in the sea water.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚由许多被称为珊瑚虫的微小动物组成，珊瑚虫用触手捕捉海水里的小型海洋生物。

sentences.en: These polyps are transparent but get their brilliant tones of pink, orange, blue, green, etc. from algae that live within them, which in turn get protection, while their photosynthesising of the sun’s rays provides nutrients for the polyps.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚虫本身是透明的，鲜艳的粉色、橙色、蓝色、绿色等来自生活在它们体内的藻类。藻类也因此受到保护，同时还能利用阳光进行光合作用，为珊瑚虫提供营养。

sentences.en: This comfortable symbiotic relationship has led to the growth of coral reefs that cover 0.1% of the planet’s ocean bed while providing homes for more than 25% of marine species, including fish, molluscs, sponges and shellfish.
sentences.zh: 这种融洽的共生关系促成了珊瑚礁的生长。珊瑚礁覆盖了全球海床面积的0.1%，却为超过25%的海洋物种提供了栖息地，包括鱼类、软体动物、海绵和有壳水生动物。

sentences.en: As a result, coral reefs are often described as the ‘rainforests of the sea’, though the comparison is dismissed by some naturalists, including David Attenborough.
sentences.zh: 因此，珊瑚礁常被称为“海洋中的雨林”。不过，包括戴维·阿滕伯勒在内的一些博物学家并不认同这种比喻。

sentences.en: ‘People say you cannot beat the rainforest,’ Attenborough has stated.
sentences.zh: 阿滕伯勒曾说：“人们都说，没有什么比得过雨林。”

sentences.en: ‘But that is simply not true.
sentences.zh: “但事实根本不是这样。

sentences.en: You go there and the first thing you think is: where … are the birds?
sentences.zh: 你到了雨林，首先想到的就是：鸟儿……在哪儿？

sentences.en: Where are the animals?
sentences.zh: 动物又在哪儿？

sentences.en: They are hiding in the trees, of course.
sentences.zh: 它们当然都藏在树丛里。

sentences.en: No, if you want beauty and wildlife, you want a coral reef.
sentences.zh: 不，如果你想欣赏美景、观赏野生生物，那就该去珊瑚礁。

sentences.en: Put on a mask and stick your head under the water.
sentences.zh: 戴上潜水面镜，把头探进水里。

sentences.en: The sight is mind-blowing.’
sentences.zh: 那景象让人震撼。”

sentences.en: Unfortunately, these majestic sights are now under very serious threat, with the most immediate problem coming in the form of thermal stress.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，这些壮丽景观如今正面临极其严重的威胁，其中最迫在眉睫的问题是热胁迫。

sentences.en: Rising ocean temperatures are triggering bleaching events that strip reefs of their colour and eventually kill them.
sentences.zh: 不断上升的海温正在引发珊瑚白化，使珊瑚礁褪去颜色，最终死亡。

sentences.en: And that is just the start.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: Other menaces include ocean acidification, sea level increase, pollution by humans, deoxygenation and ocean current changes, while the climate crisis is also increasing habitat destruction.
sentences.zh: 其他威胁包括海洋酸化、海平面上升、人为污染、海水含氧量下降和洋流变化，而气候危机也在加剧栖息地破坏。

sentences.en: As a result, vast areas – including massive chunks of Australia’s Great Barrier Reef – have already been destroyed, and scientists advise that more than 90% of reefs could be lost by 2050 unless urgent action is taken to tackle global heating and greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.zh: 结果，大片珊瑚礁已遭破坏，澳大利亚大堡礁的大片区域也在其中。科学家提醒，如果不紧急应对全球变暖和温室气体排放，到2050年可能会失去超过90%的珊瑚礁。

sentences.en: Pearce-Kelly says that coral reefs have to survive really harsh conditions – wave erosion and other factors.
sentences.zh: 皮尔斯-凯利说，珊瑚礁必须在极为恶劣的条件下生存，要承受海浪侵蚀等因素的影响。

sentences.en: And ‘when things start to go wrong in the oceans, then corals will be the first to react.
sentences.zh: 而且，“当海洋开始出问题时，珊瑚会最早作出反应。

sentences.en: And that is exactly what we are seeing now.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们现在看到的情况。

sentences.en: Coral reefs are dying and they are telling us that all is not well with our planet.’
sentences.zh: 珊瑚礁正在死亡，它们以此告诉我们，我们的地球并非一切安好。”

sentences.en: However, scientists are trying to pinpoint hardy types of coral that could survive our overheated oceans, and some of this research will be carried out at London Zoo.
sentences.zh: 不过，科学家正试图找出能在过热的海洋中生存的耐受性强的珊瑚，其中一部分研究将在伦敦动物园开展。

sentences.en: ‘Behind our … coral reef tank we have built laboratories where scientists will be studying coral species,’ said Pearce-Kelly.
sentences.zh: 皮尔斯-凯利说：“在我们的……珊瑚礁水族缸后面，建有供科学家研究珊瑚物种的实验室。”

sentences.en: One aim will be to carry out research on species to find those that can survive best in warm, acidic waters.
sentences.zh: 研究目标之一是考察不同珊瑚物种，找出最能在温暖、偏酸的水域中生存的种类。

sentences.en: Another will be to try to increase coral breeding rates.
sentences.zh: 另一个目标是设法提高珊瑚的繁殖率。

sentences.en: ‘Coral spawn just once a year,’ he added.
sentences.zh: 他补充说：“珊瑚每年只产一次卵。”

sentences.en: ‘However, aquarium-based research has enabled some corals to spawn artificially, which can assist coral reef restoration efforts.
sentences.zh: “不过，在水族馆进行的研究已使一些珊瑚能在人工条件下产卵，这有助于珊瑚礁的修复。

sentences.en: And if this can be extended for all species, we could consider the launching of coral-spawning programmes several times a year.
sentences.zh: 如果这种方法能推广到所有珊瑚物种，我们就可以考虑每年开展数次珊瑚产卵项目。

sentences.en: That would be a big help in restoring blighted reefs.’
sentences.zh: 这将对修复受损珊瑚礁大有帮助。”

sentences.en: Research in these fields is being conducted in laboratories around the world, with the London Zoo centre linked to this global network.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的实验室都在开展这些领域的研究，伦敦动物园的研究中心也是这个全球网络的一环。

sentences.en: Studies carried out in one centre can then be tested in others.
sentences.zh: 这样，在一个中心开展的研究就可以在其他中心得到检验。

sentences.en: The resulting young coral can then be displayed in the tank in Tiny Giants.
sentences.zh: 随后，培育出的幼珊瑚就能在“微小的巨人”展馆的水族缸里展出。

sentences.en: ‘The crucial point is that the progress we make in making coral better able to survive in a warming world can be shown to the public and encourage them to believe that we can do something to save the planet’s reefs,’ said Pearce-Kelly.
sentences.zh: “关键在于，我们可以让公众看到，我们在增强珊瑚在变暖的世界中生存的能力方面，已经取得了哪些进展，并鼓励他们相信，我们有办法挽救地球上的珊瑚礁，”皮尔斯-凯利说。

sentences.en: ‘Saving our coral reefs is now a critically important ecological goal.’
sentences.zh: “如今，拯救珊瑚礁是一项至关重要的生态目标。”

questions.question: Which TWO of these causes of damage to coral reefs are mentioned by the writer of the text?

options.A: a rising number of extreme storms
options.B: the removal of too many fish from the sea
options.C: the contamination of the sea from waste
options.E: alterations in the usual flow of water in the seas

questions.logic: 在威胁清单里逐项配对。C 的海水受到废物污染，对应 pollution by humans；E 的正常水流发生变化，对应 ocean current changes。海平面上升也在原文出现，但它与洋流变化是不同的现象。

questions.question: Which TWO of the following statements are true of the researchers at London Zoo?

options.A: They are hoping to expand the numbers of different corals being bred in laboratories.
options.B: They want to identify corals that can cope well with the changed sea conditions.
options.C: They are looking at ways of creating artificial reefs that corals could grow on.
options.D: They are trying out methods that would speed up reproduction in some corals.
options.E: They are investigating materials that might protect reefs from higher temperatures.

questions.logic: B 对应筛选目标，研究人员想找出在较暖、较酸海水中最能生存的珊瑚种类。D 对应繁殖目标，他们还打算设法提高珊瑚的繁殖率。题干问研究团队的工作，不能把全球珊瑚面对的威胁当作他们的研究成果。
